canonical.behaviour: Release everything on main as 2.9.2 and install it. The version changes from 2.9.1 to 2.9.2 wherever the package states it (the rules stay 1.9.0). CHANGELOG.md turns the Unreleased approval-hook entry into the 2.9.2 entry, with its known limit: an offer that a broken sibling used to hide now counts fully, so its task's open rules question can pause a write. UPGRADE.md gets a 2.9.1 to 2.9.2 section. VALIDATION.md is rewritten from a fresh full run. Then one release commit on main (the version files, the hook fix and its tests, the offer-visibility task records, and your two record lines in the bug-reproducer task) and a push. Then the Claude Code plugin is updated, and workflow-axa's Codex copies in your skills folder are replaced from the release ZIP after a full backup, checked by the installation audit; this also installs 2.9.1's two new skills there for the first time. Last, this task's evidence goes in a second small commit and push.
operations: replace the workflow-axa folders in C:/Users/Cem/.agents/skills, after a backup
exclusions: hooks/approval.py, tests/test_approval_hook.py and tests/README.md are committed as delivered, not changed
no change to how any skill or hook works beyond the delivered offer-visibility fix
no change to the user's global CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md or ARTIFACTS.md (global_policy.py and activate_rules.py --apply are not run)
no force push and no rewrite of published history
skills in ~/.agents/skills that are not workflow-axa's stay untouched
conditions: every installed folder equals the release build afterwards (diff, __pycache__ ignored)
the Codex backup is made and checked before any installed folder is replaced
the full suite and validate pass before the commit, with the known flaky lock test named if it fails
checks: audit_installation.py --check-global reports DISK_MATCH with no missing folder
full suite: python -X utf8 -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py"
